title: Future-dated version pins likely unresolvable on PyPI for CPython 3.11
description: Several pins are dated ahead of the assistant knowledge cutoff (Jan 2026) and cannot be confirmed to exist on PyPI for the documented target interpreter python3.11: torch==2.11.0 (L1), torchaudio==2.11.0 (L2), torchvision==0.26.0 (L3), transformers==5.7.0 (L6), pandas==3.0.2 (L8), matplotlib==3.10.9 (L9), scipy==1.17.1 (L12). If any of these versions does not exist for cp311, `pip install -r code/requirements.txt` (the documented bootstrap, since the repo has no venv) fails to resolve and the whole environment cannot be built. These are pinned versions in the file, NOT measured results. numpy is covered separately (DEP-002), pytest separately (DEP-003).
evidence: code/requirements.txt lines 1-3,6,8,9,12: torch==2.11.0 / torchaudio==2.11.0 / torchvision==0.26.0 / transformers==5.7.0 / pandas==3.0.2 / matplotlib==3.10.9 / scipy==1.17.1
fix: For each pin, do a resolve dry-run for cp311 (pip index versions <pkg> or pip install --dry-run) and replace any nonexistent version with the newest release that supports Python 3.11; pin the torch/torchaudio/torchvision trio to a mutually compatible published triple. Do not assert a replacement number without confirming it resolves.

title: numpy==1.26.4 is inconsistent with the rest of the stack and likely blocks resolution
description: numpy==1.26.4 (L7) is a numpy 1.x release that predates the other, future-dated pins. Modern scipy (1.17.1, L12) and pandas (3.0.2, L8) almost certainly declare numpy>=2 as a floor, so a resolver will likely reject numpy 1.26.4 alongside them and the install fails. Even if it resolved, mixing a numpy 1.x ABI with 2026-era torch/scipy binaries risks a binary-incompatibility error at import. 1.26.4 is a value literally present in the file, not a measured result.
evidence: code/requirements.txt:7 numpy==1.26.4 ; alongside code/requirements.txt:8 pandas==3.0.2 and code/requirements.txt:12 scipy==1.17.1
fix: Cross-check numpy against the numpy floors declared by the chosen scipy/pandas/torch versions; most likely bump numpy to a 2.x that satisfies all three (verify it resolves for cp311), or downgrade the whole stack consistently. Do not pin numpy independently of scipy/pandas minimums.

title: pytest>=9.0 floor may be unsatisfiable, and pytest is never imported under code/
description: pytest>=9.0 (L13). At the Jan 2026 cutoff pytest was on the 8.x series; a >=9.0 floor may not be satisfiable on PyPI, which would break the install. Separately, pytest is never imported anywhere under code/ (0 occurrences in a full grep of code/ incl. archive/); the actual pytest suites live in the repo-root tests/ directory, out of scope for code/requirements.txt. A runtime requirements file is the wrong home for a test-only tool.
evidence: code/requirements.txt:13 pytest>=9.0 ; grep for 'pytest' across code/**.py returns 0 matches
fix: Verify a pytest 9.x exists for py3.11; if not, relax to an existing floor. Consider moving pytest to a dev/test extra (e.g. requirements-dev.txt) rather than the runtime requirements.

title: Third-party 'seaborn' imported at module top level but absent from requirements.txt
description: `import seaborn as sns` runs at module import time (unguarded, top level) in four live scripts. seaborn is not declared in code/requirements.txt. After a clean install, running or importing any of these modules raises ImportError before any work begins.
evidence: code/m7_mps.py:43, code/m7_raw.py:43, code/m7_smoke_test.py:43, code/m7_trimodal_cl.py:43 each: import seaborn as sns
fix: Add seaborn (pip name: seaborn) to code/requirements.txt with a version that supports py3.11.

title: Third-party scikit-learn (import name sklearn) imported but absent from requirements.txt
description: `from sklearn.manifold import TSNE` and `from sklearn.metrics import (...)` run at module top level in four live scripts. The pip package is scikit-learn (import name sklearn) and is not declared. Clean-install import of any of these modules raises ImportError. Naming trap: the requirement must read scikit-learn, not sklearn.
evidence: code/m7_mps.py:70-71, code/m7_raw.py:62-63, code/m7_smoke_test.py:70-71, code/m7_trimodal_cl.py:70-71 (from sklearn.manifold import TSNE ; from sklearn.metrics import (...))
fix: Add scikit-learn (NOT sklearn) to code/requirements.txt with a py3.11-compatible version.

title: 'huggingface_hub' absent from requirements.txt so RULE 2 backups silently skip
description: `from huggingface_hub import HfApi` sits inside upload_to_hf() in three live scripts, and the surrounding block is wrapped in `try: ... except Exception as e: print('HF upload skipped ...')`. On a clean install (no huggingface_hub) the ImportError is swallowed: the function prints a skip message and the run continues with NO backup. RULE 2 mandates backing up to HuggingFace after every seed and the team has already lost data once, so a missing pin turns every backup into a silent no-op. Not a crash, but a research-integrity/data-loss hazard. (Note: the canonical runners m7_trimodal_run.py and m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py contain no HF code at all.)
evidence: code/m7_mps.py:2170 from huggingface_hub import HfApi ; code/m7_mps.py:2179 except Exception as e: print('  HF upload skipped ...') ; same pattern code/m7_raw.py:2147 and code/m7_trimodal_cl.py:2097
fix: Add huggingface_hub to code/requirements.txt. Additionally narrow the except so a missing backup dependency is loud (do not swallow ImportError silently), otherwise a broken RULE 2 backup is invisible.

title: Third-party 'brian2' (Brian2) imported but absent from requirements.txt
description: brian2 is imported in five archive hardware-simulation scripts and is not declared. A clean install then running any of them raises ImportError. Archive-only, but these are the Brian2/SpiNNaker verification utilities, so they are not dead in intent.
evidence: code/archive/debug_brian2_exact.py:14, code/archive/verify_brian2_raw.py:20, code/archive/verify_full.py:21, code/archive/verify_simulators.py:22, code/archive/verify_tiny.py:9 (from brian2 import ...)
fix: If these archive scripts are to remain runnable, add Brian2 (pip name: Brian2) as an optional/extra dependency (e.g. a hardware extra), not the core runtime.

title: Third-party 'PyNN' imported but absent from requirements.txt
description: `import pyNN.brian2 as sim` appears in four archive scripts; the pip package is PyNN. Not declared. Archive-only hardware-simulation path; ImportError on a clean install.
evidence: code/archive/debug_brian2_exact.py:13, code/archive/verify_full.py:20, code/archive/verify_simulators.py:21, code/archive/verify_tiny.py:8 (import pyNN.brian2 as sim)
fix: Add PyNN (pip name: PyNN) as an optional/hardware extra if these archive scripts are to remain runnable; it also pulls Brian2 (DEP-007).

title: Third-party 'wandb' imported but absent from requirements.txt (optional, guarded)
description: `import wandb` runs inside try/except ImportError with a WANDB_AVAILABLE flag in four live scripts and degrades gracefully with a printed hint. Not in the seed list; adds it. No crash, but W&B logging is silently unavailable on any clean install because the dependency is never declared.
evidence: code/m7_mps.py:83-88 try: import wandb ... except ImportError: WANDB_AVAILABLE=False ; same at code/m7_raw.py:76, code/m7_smoke_test.py:84, code/m7_trimodal_cl.py:84
fix: Declare wandb as an optional extra (e.g. a logging extra) so it is installable when W&B logging is wanted; leaving it undeclared is the reason logging never activates.

title: Declared dependencies never imported anywhere under code/
description: Four pins have zero import occurrences in a full grep of code/ (incl. archive/). transformers==5.7.0 (L6): appears only in stale notebook cruft (m7_raw.py:22 `!pip install -q transformers`; m7_mps.py:27/m7_raw.py:27/etc print 'Newly installed: ... transformers, datasets') and is never imported -> safe to drop, and it is a heavy dependency that adds resolver risk for nothing. torchaudio==2.11.0 (L2) and torchvision==0.26.0 (L3): not imported directly anywhere in code/, but are commonly transitive deps of the torch/tonic stack -> verify before removing. h5py==3.16.0 (L11): not imported directly, but tonic reads SHD from HDF5 and likely needs h5py transitively -> verify before removing. Only transformers is clearly removable.
evidence: grep across code/**.py: torchaudio 0 hits, torchvision 0 hits, h5py 0 hits, transformers only in comments/prints (m7_raw.py:22,27 ; m7_mps.py:22,27 ; m7_smoke_test.py:22,27 ; m7_trimodal_cl.py:22,27)
fix: Remove transformers unless something outside code/ needs it. For torchaudio/torchvision/h5py, confirm whether they are pulled transitively (they most likely are) and keep them if so; otherwise drop. Do not blindly delete the three transitive candidates.

title: Legacy repo-root package imports resolve only via runtime sys.path hacks plus correct CWD
description: code/ has no __init__.py, so scripts reach the repo-root legacy package (Models/, Dataloaders/, training/, utils/) by doing sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT) at runtime before importing. All referenced modules exist (Models/registry.py, training/pipeline.py, training/settings.py, Dataloaders/*_loader.py, utils/cross_modal_transfer.py), so these resolve WHEN the insert runs, but the pattern is fragile: imports must physically follow the insert (hence the noqa: E402 markers scattered through the run_* scripts), and any tool that imports the module without first running the insert (linters, IDEs, test collectors, a different CWD) fails to resolve the legacy package.
evidence: Importers of legacy packages: code/run_ablation.py:35-45 (Models.registry, training.pipeline, training.settings, Dataloaders.*) ; utils.cross_modal_transfer at code/eval_transfer_fixed.py:29, code/run_cl_rehearsal.py:44, code/run_correspondence_anchor_v2.py:45, code/run_cross_modal_alignment_study.py:61, code/run_digit_only_alignment.py:64, code/run_ordinal_anchor.py:48, code/run_rehearsal_transfer_eval_only.py:19 ; sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT)) at code/run_ablation.py and ~15 other code/ files
fix: Make the legacy package importable as a real package (pip install -e a package at repo root, or a conftest.py/path shim, or convert code/ into a package) so imports do not depend on runtime sys.path mutation and CWD.

title: Hardcoded foreign absolute path in sys.path.insert breaks repo-local imports off the origin machine
description: sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/agent1/Documents/neuromorphic/m7-trimodal-cl') hardcodes another user's directory. That path does not exist on this machine (user zainhassan; repo is at /Users/zainhassan/Documents/cross-modal-neuromorphic), so the subsequent legacy imports `from Models.registry import build_model` (line 9) and `from training.pipeline import train_step` cannot resolve -> guaranteed ImportError whenever the script is run here. It also leaks a foreign filesystem layout. Live file code/benchmark_mps_real.py plus two archive files repeat the exact literal.
evidence: code/benchmark_mps_real.py:6 sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/agent1/Documents/neuromorphic/m7-trimodal-cl') ; code/archive/benchmark_mps.py:6 (same) ; code/archive/debug_gradient.py:5 (same). benchmark_mps_real.py:9 from Models.registry import build_model
fix: Replace the hardcoded path with a portable insert such as sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)), or adopt proper packaging (see DEP-011).

title: Archive scripts compute REPO_ROOT one directory too shallow after relocation
description: REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent. For a file at code/archive/X.py this resolves to code/, not the repo root. So sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT / 'code') points to code/code/ (nonexistent) and sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT) adds code/ (not the repo root). The repo-local `from m7_trimodal_run_provenance import ...` still resolves (that module is in code/), but `from Dataloaders...` / `from utils.cross_modal_transfer...` cannot, because the legacy package lives at the repo root which is never added. These files worked before being moved into archive/; the parent.parent depth was not updated for the extra directory level.
evidence: code/archive/run_cl_confirmation.py:49 REPO_ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent ; :50-51 sys.path.insert(REPO_ROOT/'code'), sys.path.insert(REPO_ROOT) ; :204 from Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader import ... . Same shape in code/archive/run_correspondence_anchor.py:39-41 with :51 from utils.cross_modal_transfer import ...
fix: For archive-depth files use parent.parent.parent (or search upward for a repo-root marker) so REPO_ROOT is the actual repo root.

title: `import run_cl_confirmation` references a module that exists only in archive/
description: Under the --confirm CLI branch the script does `import run_cl_confirmation; run_cl_confirmation.main()`. There is no run_cl_confirmation.py in code/ (only code/run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py); the sole run_cl_confirmation.py lives in code/archive/, which is never added to sys.path (the script inserts only REPO_ROOT/'code' and REPO_ROOT). Running with --confirm therefore raises ImportError at call time. Almost certainly a stale reference left after the file was renamed/superseded by run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py.
evidence: code/run_digit_only_alignment.py:616 import run_cl_confirmation ; :617 run_cl_confirmation.main() . find shows run_cl_confirmation.py only under code/archive/ (code/ has run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py). sys.path inserts at code/run_digit_only_alignment.py:50-51
fix: Point the import at run_cl_confirmation_fixed (verify it exposes main()), or restore/relocate the intended module onto the import path.

title: Provenance shared library imports Dataloaders without setting up sys.path itself
description: m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py (the import-safe shared lib with a __main__ guard) does `from Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader import get_paired_digit_loaders` inside a function, but never inserts the repo root on sys.path itself. It works today only because every current importer (eval_transfer_fixed.py, run_cl_rehearsal.py, run_ordinal_anchor.py, etc.) runs sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT) before importing it. Invoked via its own __main__, or imported by anything that has not already fixed the path, this deferred import raises ImportError.
evidence: code/m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:1251 from Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader import get_paired_digit_loaders ; module has no sys.path.insert (grep of sys.path.insert across code/ does not list this file)
fix: Have the module ensure the repo root is importable via a guarded insert at the top (or via packaging, DEP-011); at minimum document the sys.path precondition where the __main__ block lives.

title: Stale .gitignore comment references notebooks that do not exist
description: Line 34 comment reads 'Jupyter checkpoints (keep notebooks, ignore checkpoints)', implying notebooks are tracked. Per CLAUDE.md there is no .ipynb anywhere in the repo (the M7 notebook is gone). The comment is misleading; the .ipynb_checkpoints/ rule itself is harmless.
evidence: code/.gitignore:34 '# Jupyter checkpoints (keep notebooks, ignore checkpoints)' ; :35 .ipynb_checkpoints/
fix: Drop or reword the comment so it does not imply tracked notebooks exist.

title: code/.gitignore is narrower than repo-root and ignores HDF5 globally
description: Observations, no defect. (1) code/.gitignore ignores only ICONS_M7/datasets/ (L17) and ICONS_M7/results/checkpoints/ (L21), plus *.pt/*.pth/*.ckpt/*.h5/*.hdf5 (L42-46); it does NOT ignore results CSVs or figure PNGs. Generated results are nonetheless protected because the repo-root .gitignore ignores ICONS_M7/, code/ICONS_M7 and results/. So there is redundant/overlapping coverage between the two files, and code/.gitignore ALONE would not shield a results CSV written from a different CWD. (2) The global *.h5/*.hdf5 rule (L45-46) would also exclude any legitimately tracked HDF5 fixture, should one ever be added.
evidence: code/.gitignore:16-21 (ICONS_M7/datasets/, ICONS_M7/results/checkpoints/) and :42-46 (*.pt,*.pth,*.ckpt,*.h5,*.hdf5) ; repo-root .gitignore:1-2,8-9 (ICONS_M7/, results/, code/ICONS_M7, ICONS_M7)
fix: Optional: consolidate ignore rules in one place; scope the HDF5 ignore to dataset directories if a tracked .h5 is ever needed. No action strictly required.

title: Seed-listed 'datasets' is NOT a missing dependency (it is tonic.datasets)
description: A prior audit seed listed 'datasets' among undeclared third-party imports. This is a false positive and must not be acted on. 'datasets' appears only as `from tonic import datasets, transforms` -- the datasets submodule of tonic, which IS declared (tonic==1.6.0). The HuggingFace 'datasets' package is never imported anywhere in code/; the bare token 'datasets' otherwise appears only in stale print/`!pip install` notebook cruft. Recorded so a downstream fixer does not incorrectly add the HF datasets package to requirements.
evidence: from tonic import datasets, transforms at code/m7_mps.py:67, code/m7_nmnist_smoke_test.py:16, code/m7_raw.py:59, code/m7_smoke_test.py:67, code/m7_trimodal_cl.py:67 ; no `import datasets` / `from datasets import` anywhere; tonic==1.6.0 at code/requirements.txt:5
fix: No action. Do NOT add a 'datasets' package to code/requirements.txt.
